_meta.purpose: Portable Advance Care Planning execution-rules pack. ONE source of truth shared by the Tabula EHR (Canvas plugin), PHR, and World EHR. Every jurisdiction below is a STARTER SEED and is counsel_verified:false — the engine must present it as DRAFT / pending legal review and never as legal advice. Values are conservative and must be confirmed against the current statute by counsel before any jurisdiction is presented as execution-ready.
_meta.disclaimer: This data supports document DRAFTING only. It is not legal advice. Whether a completed directive is legally valid depends on the patient meeting their own state's signing, witness, and/or notary rules at execution time. Confirm with counsel.

witness_code_legend.healthcare_agent: the person named as healthcare agent/proxy/surrogate
witness_code_legend.attending_physician: the patient's attending physician / treating clinician
witness_code_legend.facility_employee: employee/operator of the treating facility or care provider
witness_code_legend.care_provider: any healthcare provider currently caring for the patient
witness_code_legend.beneficiary: anyone entitled to any portion of the patient's estate (will or intestacy)
witness_code_legend.financially_responsible: person financially responsible for the patient's care
witness_code_legend.blood_relative: spouse or relative by blood, marriage, or adoption
witness_code_legend.signer_of_directive: a person who signs the directive on the patient's behalf

US_DEFAULT.name: Generic (conservative default)
US_DEFAULT.form_name: Advance Directive (Living Will + Healthcare Power of Attorney)
US_DEFAULT.notes: Conservative superset used when the patient's state is unknown or not yet seeded: two disinterested adult witnesses AND notarization is the safest belt-and-suspenders execution. Always defer to the patient's actual state of residence.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.statutory_citation: Va. Code §54.1-2981 et seq. (Health Care Decisions Act)

polst_program.name: POST (Physician Orders for Scope of Treatment)

VA.notes: Two adult witnesses; notarization not required by statute. Virginia authorizes electronic advance directives and remote notarization. SEED — confirm current witness-eligibility limits with counsel.

CA.name: California
CA.notes: May be executed with EITHER two qualified witnesses OR a notary. Patients in a skilled nursing facility additionally require a patient advocate or ombudsman as a witness. Health-care providers/agents are barred as witnesses. SEED — confirm with counsel.

TX.name: Texas
TX.statutory_citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code §166.031 et seq.
TX.form_name: Directive to Physicians and Family or Surrogates (+ Medical Power of Attorney)
TX.witness_qualification_note: At least ONE witness must not be any of the prohibited categories (Texas 'qualified witness' rule).
TX.notes: Directive to Physicians requires two witnesses OR notarization; at least one witness must meet the qualified-witness restrictions. Medical Power of Attorney is a separate statutory instrument. SEED — confirm with counsel.

FL.name: Florida
FL.form_name: Florida Living Will + Designation of Health Care Surrogate
FL.witness_qualification_note: At least ONE witness must be neither the patient's spouse nor a blood relative.
FL.notes: Two adult witnesses; at least one must not be a spouse or blood relative. Notarization not required. The surrogate should not act as a witness. SEED — confirm with counsel.

NY.name: New York
NY.statutory_citation: N.Y. Public Health Law Art. 29-C (Health Care Proxy)
NY.form_name: New York Health Care Proxy (+ Living Will by common law)
NY.living_will_note: New York has no living-will statute; living-will wishes are given effect under common law (Matter of O'Connor) and are best expressed alongside a statutory Health Care Proxy.
NY.notes: Health Care Proxy requires two adult witnesses; the appointed agent may not be a witness. New York uses MOLST for portable medical orders. SEED — confirm with counsel.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.statutory_citation: 755 ILCS 45/4 (Power of Attorney for Health Care) + 755 ILCS 35 (Living Will Act)
IL.form_name: Illinois Statutory Short Form Power of Attorney for Health Care (+ Living Will Declaration)
IL.notes: The statutory Power of Attorney for Health Care needs 1 disinterested witness (agent/physician disqualified); the Living Will Declaration needs 2 witnesses. Conservative floor of 2 shown. SEED — confirm with counsel.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.form_name: Pennsylvania Advance Health Care Directive (Living Will + Health Care Power of Attorney)
PA.notes: Two adult witnesses; notarization not required. The agent should not witness. SEED — confirm with counsel.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.statutory_citation: Ohio Rev. Code §2133 (Living Will) + §1337.11–.17 (Health Care POA)
OH.form_name: Ohio Living Will Declaration + Health Care Power of Attorney
OH.notes: May be executed with two disinterested witnesses OR a notary. Witnesses may not be related, the attending physician, or the agent. Ohio uses DNR Comfort Care rather than a statewide POLST. SEED — confirm with counsel.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.statutory_citation: O.C.G.A. §31-32 (Georgia Advance Directive for Health Care Act)
GA.form_name: Georgia Advance Directive for Health Care
GA.witness_qualification_note: At least one witness must not be an heir or beneficiary of the patient's estate.
GA.notes: Two witnesses; the agent and the attending physician may not witness, and at least one witness must not be an estate beneficiary. SEED — confirm with counsel.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.statutory_citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §32A-15 to -27 (Health Care POA) + §90-320 to -323 (Natural Death)
NC.form_name: North Carolina Health Care Power of Attorney + Advance Directive for a Natural Death (Living Will)

polst_program.name: North Carolina MOST (Medical Orders for Scope of Treatment)

NC.notes: North Carolina requires BOTH two qualified witnesses AND notarization. Witnesses may not be related, treating providers, estate beneficiaries, or the agent. SEED — confirm with counsel.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.form_name: Michigan Designation of Patient Advocate (Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care)

polst_program.name: Michigan Physician Orders for Scope of Treatment (MI-POST)

MI.living_will_note: Michigan has no living-will statute; end-of-life wishes are expressed through the Designation of Patient Advocate.
MI.notes: Two witnesses; witnesses may not be the patient's spouse, parent, child, grandchild, sibling, presumptive heir, physician, beneficiary, or a health-facility employee, nor the advocate. SEED — confirm with counsel.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.statutory_citation: N.J.S.A. 26:2H-53 et seq. (Advance Directives for Health Care Act)
NJ.form_name: New Jersey Advance Directive for Health Care (Proxy + Instruction Directive)
NJ.notes: Execute with either two adult witnesses OR acknowledgement before a notary/attorney/other authorized official. The agent may not witness. SEED — confirm with counsel.

WA.name: Washington
WA.statutory_citation: RCW 70.122 (Natural Death Act) + RCW 11.125 (Uniform Power of Attorney Act)
WA.form_name: Washington Health Care Directive (Living Will) + Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care
WA.notes: Health Care Directive requires two qualified witnesses; the durable power of attorney may be witnessed or notarized. Witnesses may not be treating providers, related by blood/marriage, entitled to the estate, or the agent. SEED — confirm with counsel.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.statutory_citation: A.R.S. §36-3221 (Health Care Power of Attorney) + §36-3261 (Living Will)
AZ.form_name: Arizona Health Care Power of Attorney + Living Will
AZ.notes: Arizona allows ONE qualified witness OR a notary. The witness may not be the agent, related to the patient, entitled to the estate, or involved in the patient's health care. SEED — confirm with counsel.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.living_will_note: Massachusetts has no living-will statute; the Health Care Proxy naming an agent is the operative instrument, optionally paired with a personal values/instruction statement.
MA.notes: Two adult witnesses; the agent may not witness. Massachusetts uses MOLST for portable medical orders. SEED — confirm with counsel.
